items.title: Variance-Guided Spatial Attention Fusion for Robust End-to-End Driving under Asymmetric Sensor Degradation
items.abstract: End-to-end multimodal driving has progressed rapidly by fusing camera and LiDAR streams. Existing pipelines remain fragile under asymmetric sensor degradation, where either an entire modality or only a localized region is corrupted while other regions remain useful. The key difficulty is not simply to add an uncertainty head, but to obtain dense reliability supervision, calibrate this reliability against physical fault severity, and use it before unreliable features bias the planner. We propose Variance-Guided Spatial Attention Fusion (VG-SAF), in which dense heteroscedastic reliability estimates act as interpretable spatial gates. The framework couples three components. First, a physically grounded augmentor simulates representative camera and LiDAR failures and emits a continuous spatial mask, providing dense supervision without additional annotation. Second, modality-specific experts predict per-pixel reliability scales through cross-branch dense distillation in log space, enforcing a monotone severity-to-scale response. Third, calibrated reliability maps drive a hybrid attention mechanism that suppresses unreliable cells with a local spatial gate and arbitrates between modalities through a cross-modal trust softmax. A Laplace uncertainty head emits a systemic waypoint uncertainty scale that signals severe or combined sensor degradation, including severities outside the training ranges. On the CARLA Longest6 benchmark, VG-SAF consistently improves closed-loop robustness over the baselines across camera-only, LiDAR-only, and joint degradation regimes, as measured by driving score, route completion, and infraction score.

items.llm_tldr_en: VG-SAF addresses asymmetric sensor degradation in end-to-end driving by estimating dense heteroscedastic reliability as spatial gates, coupling a physically grounded augmentor, calibration, and reliability-aware fusion before planning.
items.llm_tldr_cn: 端到端多模态融合驾驶在相机或激光雷达部分区域损坏时表现脆弱。针对这一非对称传感器退化问题，本文提出方差引导的空间注意力融合（VG-SAF），用密集的异方差可靠性估计作为可解释的空间门控。框架结合物理一致性数据增广，校准可靠性度量与物理故障严重度，并在不可靠特征影响规划前加以抑制。实验表明VG-SAF能显著提升退化场景下的驾驶规划鲁棒性，为多模态端到端驾驶提供可靠性感知的新思路。

items.title: Gripper-aware Vision Language Action Models
items.abstract: Vision language action models (VLAs) have advanced general purpose robotic grasping and manipulation by enabling robots to interpret visual observations and natural language instructions to generate executable action sequences. However, existing VLAs often implicitly assume gripper invariance, despite grasping strategies being inherently embodiment-dependent. Different gripper types, such as parallel-jaw and suction, usually require distinct interaction strategies to achieve the same grasping objective. Moreover, current datasets for VLAs predominantly rely on parallel-jaw grippers, limiting gripper-aware learning. To address this gap, we introduce MiGA, a multi-gripper-aware dataset spanning five distinct gripper types across multiple robots with 103,000 demonstrations, explicitly capturing strategy divergence under shared task objectives. We further propose GVLA, which combines a new multi-gripper tokenizer with adapter-based policy routing. Our new gripper encoding induces structured embedding information that balances parameter sharing and strategy differentiation, while layer-wise probing confirms meaningful gripper-conditioned representations for VLAs. Intensive experiments in both simulation and real-world robots show that our GVLA outperforms the current baselines across evaluated settings. Our method also improves zero-shot generalization or few-shot adaptation to new objects or unseen tasks, and enable more efficient gripper adaptation.

items.llm_tldr_cn: 现有视觉-语言-动作模型隐式假设夹爪不变，但不同夹爪类型在实现相同抓取目标时需要不同交互策略。构建包含五种夹爪、跨多机器人的MiGA数据集，共10.3万个示范，并训练夹爪感知的VLA模型。该方法让策略感知当前夹爪类型，显著提升抓取策略的灵活性与成功率，为VLA的实体相关操作提供了数据与方法基础。
